🇲🇽🏘️ <u>Renting in Mexico City: 17,000 Pesos a Month, 92,000 in Roma</u>

Average rent in Mexico City now hovers around 17,000 pesos a month, and in Colonia Roma it reaches 92,000. Landlords and real-estate firms keep adding abusive conditions, including turning away tenants who have children. Clara Brugada's Fair Rents Law would cap yearly increases at the previous year's inflation, ban discrimination against families with kids or pets, and require contracts to be registered within 30 days. Meanwhile the bankers' association ABM is asking lawmakers for "freedom" to set rents.

🇲🇽🔬 <u>IPN Tops Mexico's Patent Ranking With a Record 73</u>

Mexico's National Polytechnic Institute obtained 73 patents from IMPI in 2025. That's a record for the institute and first among all public and private universities, ahead of UNAM (53) and UANL (48). Most are in health (medical devices, drugs and vaccines), followed by energy, electronics, metallurgy and transport, backed by 1,680 IPN members of the national researchers' system.

Lázaro Cárdenas founded the IPN in 1936 so Mexico could train its own engineers. It still does.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico City Sanctions 797 Officials in One Year</u>

Mexico City's Comptroller General sanctioned 797 public servants in a year: 516 warnings, 158 suspensions, 66 disqualifications from public office and 8 dismissals, plus 47 fines worth 33.7 million pesos. Bribery, embezzlement and abuse of office are all classed as serious faults under the Administrative Responsibilities Law.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Minimum Wage 2027: Bosses Want One Digit, Unions Want 12%</u>

Mexico's 2027 minimum wage talks have opened at the Conasami wage commission, El Economista reports. Business groups led by Coparmex want the raise held to a single digit, and unions are asking for up to 12%. The general minimum is now 315.04 pesos a day, up from 88.36 in 2018. A 12% raise would take it to 352.84. The decision comes in December and takes effect January 1, when the work week also drops from 48 to 46 hours with no pay cut.

🇲🇽🎨 <u>Plan Michoacán Bets on Culture: Investment Up 250%</u>

Culture Secretary Claudia Curiel reported 163 million pesos for culture under the Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice, 250% more than in previous years. Music, performing-arts and traditional-culture festivals went from 7 to 33. More than 100 new community choirs have 5,363 children singing, and 600 instruments have been handed out. Visits to the state's archaeological sites rose 22% over 2025, to 95,000. "We coordinate 36 programs and calls for art and a culture of peace," Curiel said.

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>Ecatepec: 45,000 Families to Get Their Land Titles</u>

Ecatepec and the federal land institute INSUS will regularize 45,000 properties in the first stage of President Sheinbaum's Plan Oriente. Many are homes families have lived in for years without deeds. Thirty brigades of municipal and federal staff start in the communal lands of Guadalupe Victoria, then move on to the ejidos of Santa María Tulpetlac, Santa María Chiconautla and San Cristóbal. Plan Oriente aims to title land for more than 300,000 families across 10 State of Mexico municipalities.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico's Ambassador Rallies California's Consulates</u>

Mexico's ambassador to the US, Roberto Lazzeri, gathered the five Mexican consulates in California (Santa Ana, Los Angeles, Oxnard, San Bernardino and Fresno) in Santa Ana to overhaul how they protect Mexican nationals. The aim is a network that doesn't wait for raids to happen. The same weekend, Trump admitted his mass deportation policy had been "too harsh." "Protection of our communities requires a consular network that not only responds to emergencies, but anticipates their needs," Lazzeri said.
